statement: Wisp must recognize and validate the portable workflow contracts that connect requirements, research, specs, plans, and architecture models.
stakeholder: A coding-agent harness or developer preparing evidence-backed implementation context.
why: A spec alone cannot provide trustworthy project context; Wisp needs a version-pinned registry and canonical path rules before it can discover linked artifacts without depending on a particular harness.
done_when: The selected portable contracts are vendored byte-for-byte with source revision and SHA-256 provenance.
The library exposes contract identity, canonical artifact location, and validation for every selected version.

An additive upstream schema revision can be adopted without rejecting documents valid under the prior shape or requiring an automatic migration; validation reports the schema used without claiming the document's authoring version when the payload does not identify it.
When compatible contract versions share a canonical path, discovery validates each file once using the preferred pinned version and emits no duplicate artifact nodes.
Invalid, unknown, or incompatible contracts produce typed diagnostics without modifying canonical files.
